result:
I want to talk about how absurdly beautiful the world is when you actually slow down and look at it.

Right now, as I'm typing this, the sun is setting outside my window and the sky is doing that impossible gradient thing—electric peach melting into deep indigo, with a single contrail slicing across it like a chalk mark on a blackboard. Some bird I've never bothered to identify is doing loops in the air like it's showing off. And I'm sitting here, a hairless ape tapping on a glowing rectangle, somehow able to send my thoughts across time and space to another hairless ape who's going to read this and maybe feel something.

That's completely insane when you think about it.

I keep thinking about how most of human history would consider what we're doing right now actual magic. You're reading words that didn't exist until a few seconds ago, written by someone you've never met, possibly on a different continent, and your brain is turning these little symbols into thoughts and feelings. We're basically telepathic.

And yet we spend so much time stressed about whether our reply has the right tone or if that person liked our photo or if we're doing life "correctly."

I don't know. Sometimes I just want to grab everyone by the shoulders and say: Look. A bee figured out how to turn sunlight into honey. Octopuses can change their DNA on the fly. There's a fungus in Oregon that's been growing for 2,500 years and covers three and a half square miles. The universe is 13.8 billion years old and somehow arranged itself so that you could be here, right now, experiencing the particular flavor of existential bewilderment that is being you.

That's not nothing.

Anyway. The sky is almost dark now. The bird went home. I'm going to go make some tea and probably overthink something stupid in approximately ten minutes.

But for this one moment, I'm just glad we're all here being ridiculous together.

What are you looking at right now? Tell me something beautiful you've noticed lately.
